findings.title: Park24 first report: possible personal information leak from unauthorized access to the Times Car website (Report 1)
findings.summary_md: Park24's first public statement on the incident, published September 25, 2026 at 20:30 JST per the company RSS feed. It says unauthorized access to the Times Car web system was detected at 09:07 JST that day, and per a September 26 addendum the intrusion path was severed and attack-source communications blocked, with post-block inaccessibility confirmed, by 07:25 JST. The notice already listed the potentially leaked categories (name, address, date of birth, phone, email, member number, license information, identity verification documents, corporate member data, linked service IDs), reported the matter to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission, and warned members to expect impersonation phishing, with a 24-hour hotline at 0120-25-8924.

findings.title: Park24 second report: investigation results and response for unauthorized access to the Times Car web system (Report 2)
findings.summary_md: Park24's second report, published September 28, 2026 at 13:30 JST per the company RSS feed, roughly 16 hours before the BleepingComputer story. It confirms data stored on the breached system was obtained by a third party for about 6.6 million accounts, a figure that includes current and former Times Car members, Times Business Service corporate members, and people whose enrollment never completed. Passwords were stored in a form the company says cannot be restored, credit card data was not leaked, and the linked service IDs cover nine services including JR West's WESTER ID. Park24 reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission and police, is running forensics with an external specialist, and said individual notifications would follow.
